title: Ensure mariadb is Not Started With 'skip-grant-tables'
description: This option causes mariadbd to start without using the privilege system. Counts enabled skip-grant-tables settings in the server option groups and on the running server command line.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure mariadb is Not Started With 'skip-grant-tables'

audit.command:
c=$(my_print_defaults --mysqld 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(ps -eo comm=,args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=$( { printf '%s
' "$c"; printf '%s
' "$p" | awk '$1=="mysqld"||$1=="mariadbd"' | tr ' ' '
'; } | grep -Eic '^--skip[-_]grant[-_]tables(=(1|on|true|yes))?$' ); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove skip-grant-tables (and skip_grant_tables) from the option files or set skip-grant-tables = FALSE, remove it from the start-up command line, and restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure strong authentication is utilized for all accounts
description: The mysql_native_password and mysql_old_password plugins utilize weak cryptography and/or weak password routines. In particular, the mysql_old_password plugin utilizes cracked password routines and is subject to Pass-the-Hash attacks. The mysql_native_password plugin relies on the Secure Hash Algorithm 1 (SHA-1) algorithm. Counts accounts still using mysql_native_password/mysql_old_password/no plugin, apart from root and mysql with an invalid password string. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3 Ensure strong authentication is utilized for all accounts

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE plugin IN ('mysql_native_password', 'mysql_old_password', '') AND NOT (User = 'root' AND authentication_string = 'invalid') AND NOT (User = 'mysql' AND authentication_string = 'invalid')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED VIA unix_socket; SET PASSWORD FOR 'mysql'@'localhost' = 'invalid'; SET PASSWORD FOR 'mariadb.sys'@'localhost' = 'invalid'; and move every other listed account to ed25519, gssapi, pam or unix_socket (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED VIA ed25519 USING PASSWORD('...')).

title: Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for MariaDB Daemon/Service
description: As with any service installed on a host, it can be provided with its own user context. Providing a dedicated user to the service provides the ability to precisely constrain the service within the larger host context. Passes when the running mariadbd/mysqld process does not run as root (the benchmark expects the mysql account).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Use Dedicated Least Privileged Account for MariaDB Daemon/Service

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user:32=,comm= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2=="mysqld"||$2=="mariadbd"{n++; if($1=="root")r++} END{if(!n)print "not-running"; else if(r)print "runs-as-root"; else print "compliant"}'

remediation.command: Run MariaDB under a dedicated unprivileged account (normally mysql, no sudo rights, shell /bin/false): groupadd -r mysql; useradd -r -M -g mysql -d /var/lib/mysql -s /bin/false mysql; set user=mysql under [mariadbd] or User=mysql in the systemd unit, then restart.

title: Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions
description: MariaDB supports multiple versions of TLS. The higher the version the stronger the security and/or better the performance. The MariaDB 10.11 default (TLSv1.1,TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3) fails. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.10 Limit Accepted Transport Layer Security (TLS) Versions

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(FIND_IN_SET('TLSv1.0', @@global.tls_version) = 0 AND FIND_IN_SET('TLSv1.1', @@global.tls_version) = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set tls_version=TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3 under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure 'datadir' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: The data directory is the location of the MariaDB databases. Expects drwxr-x--- mysql:mysql (0700 also accepted); run as root on the database host. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure 'datadir' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$d" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$s" in "750 mysql mysql"|"700 mysql mysql") echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

title: Ensure SSL Key Files Have Appropriate Permissions
description: When configured to use SSL/TLS, MariaDB relies on Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) key files, which are stored on the host's filesystem. These SSL key files are subject to the host's permissions and ownership structure. Every file named by an ssl_ca/ssl_cert/ssl_key/ssl_crl variable must be -r-------- mysql:mysql (directories in ssl_capath/ssl_crlpath are skipped). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.7 Ensure SSL Key Files Have Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; l=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) REGEXP '^.*ssl_(ca|capath|cert|crl|crlpath|key)\$' AND VARIABLE_VALUE <> ''" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=0; for f in $l; do case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; [ -f "$f" ] || continue; [ "$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$f")" = "400 mysql mysql" ] || n=$((n+1)); done; [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chown mysql:mysql <ssl_file> && chmod 400 <ssl_file> for every ssl_ca/ssl_cert/ssl_key/ssl_crl file in use.

title: Ensure Plugin Directory Has Appropriate Permissions
description: The plugin directory is the location of the MariaDB plugins. Plugins are storage engines or user defined functions (UDFs). Expects plugin_dir mode 550 or 554. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.8 Ensure Plugin Directory Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; p=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.plugin_dir, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; m=$(stat -c %a "$p" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$m" in 550|554) echo compliant ;; *) echo "mode $m" ;; esac

remediation.command: chmod 550 <plugin_dir> (or 554) && chown mysql:mysql <plugin_dir>; the server must not be able to write to it.

title: Ensure File Key Management Encryption Plugin files have appropriate permissions
description: Certain Key Management Encryption plugins must store sensitive information in files for later retrieval. Such files should have proper permissions. Reads file_key_management_filename/filekey from the server option groups; fails when the plugin is not configured or a key file is not mysql:mysql with mode 750 or stricter.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.10 Ensure File Key Management Encryption Plugin files have appropriate permissions

audit.command: c=$(my_print_defaults --mysqld 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; fn=$(printf '%s\n' "$c" | sed -n 's/^--file[-_]key[-_]management[-_]filename=//p' | tail -n 1); fk=$(printf '%s\n' "$c" | sed -n 's/^--file[-_]key[-_]management[-_]filekey=//p' | tail -n 1); [ -n "$fn" ] || { echo "file_key_management not configured"; exit 0; }; [ -f "$fn" ] || { echo "missing $fn"; exit 0; }; n=0; for x in "$fn" "${fk#FILE:}"; do [ -n "$x" ] && [ -f "$x" ] || continue; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$x"); m=${s%% *}; [ "${s#* }" = "mysql mysql" ] && [ $((0$m & 027)) -eq 0 ] || n=$((n+1)); done; [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chmod 750 <file> (or stricter, e.g. 640/600) && chown mysql:mysql <file> for file_key_management_filename and a FILE: file_key_management_filekey; if the plugin is not configured, implement data-at-rest encryption first (4.9).

title: Ensure the Latest Security Patches are Applied
description: Periodically, updates to MariaDB server are released to resolve bugs, mitigate vulnerabilities, and provide new features. It is recommended that MariaDB installations are up to date with the latest security updates.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure the Latest Security Patches are Applied

audit.command: Run SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name LIKE 'version'; and compare with the latest release and security announcements from MariaDB and your OS vendor. An outdated release is a fail.

remediation.command: Upgrade MariaDB to the latest release of the installed series with the package manager during a maintenance window and run the upgrade steps for the release.

title: Ensure Only Administrative Users Have Full Database Access
description: The mysql.user, mysql.db, and other mysql tables ending in _priv list a variety of privileges that can be granted (or denied) to MariaDB users. Some of the privileges of concern include: Select_priv, Insert_priv, Update_priv, Delete_priv, Drop_priv, and so on.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure Only Administrative Users Have Full Database Access

audit.command: Run SELECT * FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE grantee NOT LIKE ('\'mysql.%localhost\''); and ensure all returned users are administrative users with the minimal privileges required.

remediation.command: REVOKE unnecessary privileges (e.g. REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>';) and GRANT only database-level privileges that are needed.

title: Ensure 'FILE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The FILE privilege is used to allow or disallow a user from reading and writing files on the server host. Any user with the FILE right granted has the ability to: ; Read files from the local file system that are readable by the MariaDB server (this includes world-readable files). ; Write files to the local file system where the MariaDB server has write access.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure 'FILE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'FILE'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE FILE ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The SUPER privilege is a powerful and far-reaching privilege and should not be granted lightly. In MariaDB, SUPER is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of MariaDB. The SUPER privilege shown in the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES table governs the use of a variety of MariaDB features.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure 'SUPER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'SUPER'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The CREATE USER privilege governs the right of a given user to add or remove users, change existing users' names, or revoke existing users' privileges.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.6 Ensure 'CREATE USER' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'CREATE USER'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE CREATE USER ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'GRANT OPTION' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The GRANT OPTION privilege exists in different contexts (mysql.user, mysql.db) for the purpose of governing the ability of a privileged user to manipulate the privileges of other users.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.7 Ensure 'GRANT OPTION' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT DISTINCT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE IS_GRANTABLE = 'YES'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE GRANT OPTION ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure Audit Logging Is Enabled
description: Enabling audit logging is an important consideration for a production environment, and MariaDB plugin exist to help with this. Enable audit logging for ; Connect events ; Query and Table events (optional) Requires the server_audit plugin with server_audit_logging=ON and CONNECT events audited (an empty server_audit_events audits everything). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4 Ensure Audit Logging Is Enabled

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF((SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'server_audit_logging') = 'ON' AND ((SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'server_audit_events') = '' OR FIND_IN_SET('CONNECT', (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'server_audit_events')) > 0), 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Under [mariadbd] add plugin_load_add = server_audit, server_audit_logging=ON and server_audit_events=CONNECT (optionally QUERY_DDL,QUERY_DCL,TABLE), then restart MariaDB.

title: Disable use of the mysql_old_password plugin
description: The mysql_old_password plugin uses a cracked password routine with several flaws. It is present but not used by default in MariaDB. Steps should be taken to ensure that passwords will not be created with this plugin and that clients will not be able to authenticate to the MariaDB server using this plugin. Requires old_passwords OFF and secure_auth ON. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.1 Disable use of the mysql_old_password plugin

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.old_passwords = 0 AND @@global.secure_auth = 1, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set old_passwords=0 and secure_auth=ON under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure Passwords are Not Stored in the Global Configuration
description: The [client] section of the MariaDB configuration file allows setting a user and password to be used. Verify the password option is not used in the global configuration file (mariadb.cnf). Reads the [client] groups of /etc/my.cnf and /etc/mysql/my.cnf (including !include files) with my_print_defaults; per-user ~/.my.cnf files are not global and are ignored.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2 Ensure Passwords are Not Stored in the Global Configuration

audit.command: n=0; found=0; for c in /etc/my.cnf /etc/mysql/my.cnf; do [ -f "$c" ] || continue; found=1; o=$(my_print_defaults --defaults-file="$c" client client-server client-mariadb 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=$((n + $(printf '%s\n' "$o" | grep -c '^--password'))); done; [ "$found" -eq 1 ] || exit 1; echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove password= from the [client] section of the global option files; use a per-user ~/.my.cnf with mode 0600 instead.

title: Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place
description: Passwords should be configured with a minimum length of 14 characters and should be checked against dictionaries of common, known, and expected passwords. Requires simple_password_check and cracklib_password_check ACTIVE with FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT, simple_password_check_minimal_length >= 14 and strict_password_validation ON (the dictionary contents are not checked). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.4 Ensure Password Complexity Policies are in Place

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE LOWER(PLUGIN_NAME) IN ('simple_password_check', 'cracklib_password_check') AND PLUGIN_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND LOAD_OPTION = 'FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT') = 2 AND (SELECT VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE LOWER(VARIABLE_NAME) = 'simple_password_check_minimal_length') >= 14 AND @@global.strict_password_validation = 1, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Install the plugins (INSTALL SONAME 'simple_password_check'; INSTALL SONAME 'cracklib_password_check'; the cracklib plugin may need an OS package) and add under [mariadbd]: plugin_load_add = simple_password_check, simple_password_check = FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT, simple_password_check_minimal_length = 14, plugin_load_add = cracklib_password_check, cracklib_password_check = FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT, strict_password_validation = ON; restart.

title: Ensure No Anonymous Accounts Exist
description: Anonymous accounts are users with empty usernames (''). Anonymous accounts have no passwords, so anyone can use them to connect to the MariaDB server. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.6 Ensure No Anonymous Accounts Exist

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE user = ''" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: DROP USER ''@'<host>'; for each anonymous account (or run mariadb-secure-installation).

title: Ensure 'require_secure_transport' is Set to 'ON' and 'have_ssl' is Set to 'YES'
description: All network traffic must use SSL/TLS when traveling over untrusted networks. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.1 Ensure 'require_secure_transport' is Set to 'ON' and 'have_ssl' is Set to 'YES'

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.require_secure_transport = 1 AND @@global.have_ssl = 'YES', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Configure TLS (ssl_cert, ssl_key, ssl_ca under [mariadbd]) so have_ssl = YES, confirm all clients use TLS, then set require_secure_transport=ON under [mariadbd] and restart (or SET GLOBAL require_secure_transport = ON).

title: Ensure 'ssl_type' is Set to 'ANY', 'X509', or 'SPECIFIED' for All Remote Users
description: All network traffic must use SSL/TLS when traveling over untrusted networks. SSL/TLS should be enforced on a per-user basis for users which enter the system through the network. Counts remote accounts whose ssl_type is not ANY, X509 or SPECIFIED. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.2 Ensure 'ssl_type' is Set to 'ANY', 'X509', or 'SPECIFIED' for All Remote Users

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE host NOT IN ('::1', '127.0.0.1', 'localhost') AND ssl_type NOT IN ('ANY', 'X509', 'SPECIFIED')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' REQUIRE X509; (or REQUIRE SSL / ISSUER / SUBJECT) for every remote account listed by SELECT user, host, ssl_type FROM mysql.user WHERE host NOT IN ('::1','127.0.0.1','localhost');

title: Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured
description: The replication traffic between servers should be secured. Security measures should include ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of the traffic and performing mutual authentication between the servers before performing replication.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.1 Ensure Replication Traffic is Secured

audit.command: Check that replication traffic uses a private network, a VPN, SSL/TLS or an SSH tunnel for confidentiality, integrity and mutual server authentication. If using TLS, run SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G and verify Master_SSL_Allowed = Yes.

remediation.command: Secure replication with TLS (CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_SSL=1, MASTER_SSL_CA=... and REQUIRE SSL/X509 for the replication account) or a private network/VPN.

title: Ensure 'MASTER_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT' is enabled
description: On the MariaDB REPLICA, the setting MASTER_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT indicates whether the REPLICA should perform server certificate verification of the PRIMARY's certificate. Checks every replication connection in SHOW ALL REPLICAS STATUS; passes on servers that are not replicas. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.2 Ensure 'MASTER_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -Ee "SHOW ALL REPLICAS STATUS" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F': ' '/Master_SSL_Verify_Server_Cert:/{if($2!="Yes")b++} END{print b?"noncompliant":"compliant"}'

remediation.command: STOP REPLICA; CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_SSL_VERIFY_SERVER_CERT = 1; START REPLICA; (per connection name for multi-source replication).

title: Ensure 'super_priv' is Not Set to 'Y' for Replication Users
description: The SUPER privilege found in the mysql.user table governs the use of a variety of MariaDB features. These features include, CHANGE MASTER TO, KILL, mysqladmin kill option, PURGE BINARY LOGS, SET GLOBAL, mysqladmin debug option, logging control, and more. Treats every account other than root and mysql (the MariaDB system administrator accounts) holding REPLICATION SLAVE as a replication user and counts those that also hold SUPER. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.3 Ensure 'super_priv' is Not Set to 'Y' for Replication Users

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE Repl_slave_priv = 'Y' AND Super_priv = 'Y' AND user NOT IN ('root', 'mysql')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: REVOKE SUPER ON *.* FROM '<repl user>'@'<host>';

title: Ensure mutual TLS is enabled
description: Mutual TLS (a.k.a. Two-Way TLS) enhances TLS by requiring that both parties authenticate each other when establishing a connection. Mutual TLS adds a requirement (over TLS) that the client provide its certificate so the server can authenticate the client.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.5 Ensure mutual TLS is enabled

audit.command: If replication uses TLS, run SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G on the replica and verify Master_SSL_Cert and Master_SSL_Key name the replica's certificate and key; on the primary verify the replication account requires a certificate (SELECT user, host, ssl_type FROM mysql.user WHERE Repl_slave_priv = 'Y'; ssl_type X509 or SPECIFIED).

remediation.command: On the replica: CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_SSL_CERT = '<cert>', MASTER_SSL_KEY = '<key>', MASTER_SSL_CA = '<ca>'; on the primary: ALTER USER '<repl>'@'<host>' REQUIRE X509;

title: Verify That the MYSQL_PWD Environment Variable is Not in Use
description: MariaDB can read a default database password from an environment variable called MYSQL_PWD. Avoiding use of this environment variable can better safeguard the confidentiality of MariaDB credentials. Run as root; counts processes whose environment contains MYSQL_PWD (including the scanner itself if it was given MYSQL_PWD).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Verify That the MYSQL_PWD Environment Variable is Not in Use

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -lsaz '^MYSQL_PWD=' /proc/[0-9]*/environ 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Find the processes (grep -lsaz ^MYSQL_PWD= /proc/*/environ) and change the users/scripts that export MYSQL_PWD to use an option file readable only by the user or certificate-based authentication.

title: Ensure Interactive Login is Disabled
description: When created, the MariaDB user may have interactive access to the operating system, which means that the MariaDB user could login to the host as any other user would. Checks that the mysql account has /bin/false or nologin as its shell.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure Interactive Login is Disabled

audit.command: out=$(getent passwd mysql 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; s=${out##*:}; case "$s" in /bin/false|/usr/bin/false|/sbin/nologin|/usr/sbin/nologin) echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

remediation.command: usermod -s /bin/false mysql

title: Verify That 'MYSQL_PWD' is Not Set in Users' Profiles
description: MariaDB can read a default database password from an environment variable called MYSQL_PWD. Run as root; counts Bash login scripts in /home/*, /root and /etc/environment that mention MYSQL_PWD.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Verify That 'MYSQL_PWD' is Not Set in Users' Profiles

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -ls MYSQL_PWD /home/*/.bashrc /home/*/.profile /home/*/.bash_profile /root/.bashrc /root/.profile /root/.bash_profile /etc/environment 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$n"

remediation.guidance: Remove MYSQL_PWD from the listed login scripts and use a protected option file (~/.my.cnf, mode 0600) instead.

title: Backup Policy in Place
description: A backup policy should be in place.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.1 Backup Policy in Place

audit.command: Check that a backup schedule exists (crontab -l for the backup user, systemd timers or the backup tool scheduler) covering all databases.

remediation.command: Define and schedule regular full and incremental backups (mariadb-backup), e.g. via cron or systemd timers.

title: Verify Backups are Good
description: Backups should be validated on a regular basis.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.2 Verify Backups are Good

audit.command: Check reports of backup validation tests: backups must be restored regularly to a test system and verified.

remediation.command: Implement a regular restore test of backups and keep the validation reports.

title: Secure Backup Credentials
description: A database user with the least amount of privileges required to perform backup is needed. The credentials for this user should be protected. The password, certificate, and any other credentials should be protected.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.3 Secure Backup Credentials

audit.command: Check permissions of files containing backup passwords and/or SSL keys (ls -l on option files and key files used by backup jobs); they must be readable only by the backup account.

remediation.command: chmod 600 the files holding backup credentials/keys and chown them to the backup user; prefer an option file over passwords on the command line.

title: The Backups Should be Properly Secured
description: The backup files will contain all data in the databases. Filesystem permissions and/or encryption should be used to prevent unauthorized users from gaining access to the backups.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.4 The Backups Should be Properly Secured

audit.command: Check who can access backup files: they must not be world-readable or in a world-readable directory, group access only for a backup-specific group, offsite copies restricted, and backups encrypted with a key stored separately (not a guessable password).

remediation.command: Restrict backup files and directories (e.g. chmod 600/700, backup-specific owner/group), encrypt backups, and store the encryption key separately from the backups.

title: Point-in-Time Recovery
description: With binlogs it is possible to implement point-in-time recovery. This makes it possible to restore the changes between the last full backup and the point-in-time. Enabling binlogs is not sufficient. The binlogs need to be backed up to separate media. The restore procedure should be created and tested. Passes when binary logging is enabled and binlog_expire_logs_seconds is not 0. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.5 Point-in-Time Recovery

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.log_bin = 1 AND @@global.binlog_expire_logs_seconds <> 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set log_bin=<path> and binlog_expire_logs_seconds=<retention seconds, not 0> under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then create and test a point-in-time restore procedure, then restart MariaDB.

title: Disaster Recovery (DR) Plan
description: A disaster recovery plan should be created. MariaDB Galera Cluster (group replication), MariaDB Replication (asynchronous replication) or both may be used. A replica in a different data center and offsite backups may be used.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.6 Disaster Recovery (DR) Plan

audit.command: Check that a documented disaster recovery plan exists (e.g. a replica in another data center or offsite backups), including recovery time objectives and tested procedures.

remediation.command: Create and test a disaster recovery plan (offsite backups, replicas in a separate location, documented restore steps).

title: Do Not Specify Passwords in the Command Line
description: When a command is executed on the command line, for example mariadb -u admin -p password, the password may be visible in the user's shell/command history or in the process list.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Do Not Specify Passwords in the Command Line

audit.command: Check the process list (ps -ef) and shell histories for mariadb/mysqldump invocations with -p<password> or --password=<password>. Any visible password is a fail.

remediation.command: Use -p without a value (prompt), an option file with mode 0600 instead of passwords on the command line, and clear exposed history entries.

title: Ensure Non-Default, Unique Cryptographic Material is in Use
description: The cryptographic material used by MariaDB, such as digital certificates and encryption keys, should be used only for MariaDB and only for one instance. Default cryptographic material should not be used since it is not unique to the instance.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5 Ensure Non-Default, Unique Cryptographic Material is in Use

audit.command: Review all cryptographic material: openssl x509 -in <datadir or ssl_cert>/server-cert.pem -subject -noout | grep Auto_Generated_Server_Certificate. Any output (auto-generated cert) or material shared with other instances/purposes is a finding.

remediation.command: Issue a unique certificate and key from your CA for this instance, set ssl_cert/ssl_key/ssl_ca under [mariadbd], and restart or run ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS (MariaDB: FLUSH SSL).

title: Ensure 'password_lifetime' is Less Than or Equal to '365'
description: Password expiration provides users with a unique time bounded password lifetime. Fails when default_password_lifetime exceeds 365 or an account in mysql.global_priv overrides it with 0 (never) or more than 365 days. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6 Ensure 'password_lifetime' is Less Than or Equal to '365'

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.default_password_lifetime <= 365 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.global_priv WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(Priv, '\$.password_lifetime') = 0 OR JSON_EXTRACT(Priv, '\$.password_lifetime') > 365) = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: SET GLOBAL default_password_lifetime = 365; add default_password_lifetime=365 under [mariadbd], and fix per-account overrides with ALTER USER <user>@<host> PASSWORD EXPIRE INTERVAL 365 DAY;

title: Lock Out Accounts if Not Currently in Use
description: If users with accounts will not be using their account for some time, to reduce the risk of attacks or inappropriate account usage or if suspicions exist that an account might be under attack, disabling the account will secure it and once it's ready to resume use it can easily be re-enabled.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7 Lock Out Accounts if Not Currently in Use

audit.command: Review lock status: SELECT CONCAT(user, '@', host, ' => ', JSON_DETAILED(priv)) FROM mysql.global_priv; Accounts not in use and reserved accounts must show account_locked:true.

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' ACCOUNT LOCK; for each unused account (ACCOUNT UNLOCK when needed again).

title: Ensure Socket Peer-Credential Authentication is Used Appropriately
description: The server-side unix_socket authentication plugin authenticates clients that connect to the MariaDB server from the local host through the Unix socket file. Users authenticated using unix_socket need not specify a password when connecting to the server.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.8 Ensure Socket Peer-Credential Authentication is Used Appropriately

audit.command: Run SELECT PLUGIN_NAME, PLUGIN_STATUS FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_NAME = 'unix_socket'; and SELECT CONCAT(user,'@',host,' => ',JSON_DETAILED(priv)) FROM mysql.global_priv WHERE JSON_CONTAINS(priv, '{"plugin":"unix_socket"}', '$.auth_or'); Use of the plugin when not allowed, a non-localhost host or an unauthorized user is a fail.

remediation.command: Restrict unix_socket to authorized local accounts (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED VIA ...), or disable the plugin with unix_socket=OFF under [mariadbd] if your policy forbids it.

title: Ensure MariaDB is Bound to One or More Specific IP Addresses
description: By default, the MariaDB server accepts TCP/IP connections from MariaDB user accounts on all server host IPv6 and IPv4 interfaces. You can make this configuration more restrictive by setting the bind_address configuration option to one or more specific IPv4 or IPv6 addresses so that the server only accepts TCP/IP connections on those addresses. Fails when bind_address is empty, '*', '::' or '0.0.0.0' (all interfaces). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.9 Ensure MariaDB is Bound to One or More Specific IP Addresses

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(IFNULL(@@global.bind_address, '') NOT IN ('', '*', '::', '0.0.0.0'), 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set bind_address=<specific IP> (comma-separated list for several addresses) under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Require Client-Side Certificates (X.509)
description: Client-side certificates may be used as proof of identity. Counts accounts other than mysql, root and mariadb.sys that do not require a client certificate (ssl_type X509 or SPECIFIED). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.11 Require Client-Side Certificates (X.509)

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT IN ('mysql', 'root', 'mariadb.sys') AND ssl_type NOT IN ('X509', 'SPECIFIED')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' REQUIRE X509; for each account; clients then connect with --ssl-cert, --ssl-key and --ssl-ca.

title: Ensure Only Approved Ciphers are Used
description: MariaDB supports multiple encryption ciphers. Ciphers can vary in strength, speed and overhead. Automates the benchmark's failure on an empty ssl_cipher; whether the configured list contains only approved ciphers still needs review. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.12 Ensure Only Approved Ciphers are Used

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(IFNULL(@@global.ssl_cipher, '') <> '', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set ssl_cipher='ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' (or another approved list) under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure 'log_bin_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions
description: MariaDB can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log, general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Fails when any <log_bin_basename>.* file grants other users access, is executable or is not owned by mysql:mysql (benchmark: -rw-rw---- mysql mysql); passes when binary logging is off. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure 'log_bin_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.log_bin_basename, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$b" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; case "$b" in /*) ;; *) b="$d/${b#./}" ;; esac; [ -d "$(dirname "$b")" ] || exit 1; n=$(find "$(dirname "$b")" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$(basename "$b").*" \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \) | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chmod 660 <log_bin_basename>.* && chown mysql:mysql <log_bin_basename>.*

title: Ensure 'log_error' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MariaDB can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log, general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Expects the error log file (relative paths resolve to datadir) to be -rw------- mysql:mysql; logging to stderr only fails (see 6.1). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure 'log_error' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; f=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.log_error, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$f" in ""|stderr|*stderr.err) echo "no log file"; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$s" in "600 mysql mysql") echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

remediation.command: chmod 600 <log_error> && chown mysql:mysql <log_error>

title: Ensure 'slow_query_log' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MariaDB can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log, general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Passes when the slow query log is off; otherwise the file must not be accessible to other users, executable, or owned by anyone but mysql:mysql. Remove old slow log files manually. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure 'slow_query_log' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; on=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.slow_query_log + 0, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ "$on" = 0 ] && { echo compliant; exit 0; }; f=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.slow_query_log_file, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; [ -f "$f" ] || exit 1; [ -z "$(find "$f" -maxdepth 0 \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \))" ] && echo compliant || echo "bad permissions on $f"

remediation.command: Disable the slow query log (SET GLOBAL slow_query_log = OFF and slow_query_log=0 under [mariadbd]); if it must stay on: chmod 660 <slow_query_log_file> && chown mysql:mysql <slow_query_log_file>.

title: Ensure 'relay_log_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions
description: MariaDB can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log (which can be encrypted), general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Fails when any <relay_log_basename>.* file grants other users access, is executable or is not owned by mysql:mysql. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.5 Ensure 'relay_log_basename' Files Have Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.relay_log_basename, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$b" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; case "$b" in /*) ;; *) b="$d/${b#./}" ;; esac; [ -d "$(dirname "$b")" ] || exit 1; n=$(find "$(dirname "$b")" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$(basename "$b").*" \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \) | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$n noncompliant files"

remediation.command: chmod 660 <relay_log_basename>.* && chown mysql:mysql <relay_log_basename>.*

title: Ensure 'general_log_file' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MariaDB can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log (which can be encrypted), error log, slow query log, relay log (which can be encrypted), general log, and in the enterprise edition, the audit log (which can be encrypted). Passes when the general log is off and no old file remains, or when it is on and the file is -rw------- mysql:mysql. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.6 Ensure 'general_log_file' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; on=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.general_log + 0, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; f=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.general_log_file, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; if [ "$on" = 0 ]; then [ -e "$f" ] && echo "general log disabled but old file $f exists" || echo compliant; exit 0; fi; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ "$s" = "600 mysql mysql" ] && echo compliant || echo "$s"

remediation.command: Disable the general log (SET GLOBAL general_log = OFF and general_log=0 under [mariadbd]) and remove old general log files; if it must stay on: chmod 600 <general_log_file> && chown mysql:mysql <general_log_file>.

title: Ensure 'server_audit_file_path' Has Appropriate Permissions
description: MariaDB can operate using a variety of log files, each used for different purposes. These are the binary log, error log, slow query log, relay log, audit log and general log. Because these are files on the host operating system, they are subject to the permissions and ownership structure provided by the host and may be accessible by users other than the mysql user. Fails when the server_audit plugin is not loaded (no server_audit_file_path); otherwise the audit file (relative paths resolve to datadir) must not be accessible to other users, executable, or owned by anyone but mysql:mysql. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.9 Ensure 'server_audit_file_path' Has Appropriate Permissions

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; f=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.server_audit_file_path" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$f" ] || exit 1; case "$f" in /*) ;; *) f="$d/${f#./}" ;; esac; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "missing $f"; exit 0; }; [ -z "$(find "$f" -maxdepth 0 \( -perm /0117 -o ! -user mysql -o ! -group mysql \))" ] && echo compliant || echo "bad permissions on $f"

remediation.command: chmod 660 <server_audit_file_path> && chown mysql:mysql <server_audit_file_path>

title: Ensure Example or Test Databases are Not Installed on Production Servers
description: The default MariaDB installation does not contain any example or test databases. However, it is a good idea to review for common example databases and ensure they have been removed from production systems. Counts the common example databases (test, employees, world, world_x, sakila, airportdb, menagerie). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure Example or Test Databases are Not Installed on Production Servers

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME IN ('test','employees','world','world_x','sakila','airportdb','menagerie')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: DROP DATABASE <name>; for each example/test database on a production server.

title: Ensure 'allow-suspicious-udfs' is Set to 'OFF'
description: This option prevents attaching arbitrary shared library functions as user-defined functions by checking for at least one corresponding method named _init, _deinit, _reset, _clear, or _add. Counts allow-suspicious-udfs settings in the server option groups (my_print_defaults --mysqld) and on the running server command line.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure 'allow-suspicious-udfs' is Set to 'OFF'

audit.command:
c=$(my_print_defaults --mysqld 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(ps -eo comm=,args= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; n=$( { printf '%s
' "$c"; printf '%s
' "$p" | awk '$1=="mysqld"||$1=="mariadbd"' | tr ' ' '
'; } | grep -Eic '^--allow[-_]suspicious[-_]udfs(=(1|on|true|yes))?$' ); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove allow-suspicious-udfs from the MariaDB option files and from the server start-up command line, then restart.

title: Harden Usage for 'local_infile' on MariaDB Clients
description: The local_infile parameter dictates whether files located on the MariaDB client's computer can be loaded or selected via LOAD DATA INFILE or SELECT local_file. Checks the server-side branch of the benchmark (local_infile = 0); if LOAD DATA LOCAL is required, use clients 10.2.0+ with --load-data-local-dir and accept the finding as an exception. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Harden Usage for 'local_infile' on MariaDB Clients

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.local_infile = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: SET GLOBAL local_infile = 0; and add local-infile=0 under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf).

title: Ensure Symbolic Links are Disabled
description: The symbolic-links and skip-symbolic-links options for MariaDB determine whether symbolic link support is available. When use of symbolic links is enabled, they have different effects depending on the host platform. When symbolic links are disabled, then symbolic links stored in files or entries in tables are not used by the database. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.6 Ensure Symbolic Links are Disabled

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.have_symlink = 'DISABLED', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set skip-symbolic-links=YES under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure the 'secure_file_priv' is Configured Correctly
description: The secure_file_priv option restricts to paths used by LOAD DATA INFILE or SELECT local_file. It is recommended that this option be set to a file system location that contains only resources expected to be loaded by MariaDB. Fails only when secure_file_priv is an empty string (import/export allowed everywhere). Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.7 Ensure the 'secure_file_priv' is Configured Correctly

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.secure_file_priv IS NULL OR @@global.secure_file_priv <> '', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set secure_file_priv=<path_to_load_directory> (or remove the empty setting) under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Enable data-at-rest encryption in MariaDB
description: Data-at-rest encryption protects the privacy of your information, prevents data breaches and helps meet regulatory requirements. Fails when any *ENCRYPT* server variable is OFF, or InnoDB reports no tablespaces or any unencrypted tablespace in INNODB_TABLESPACES_ENCRYPTION. Backup encryption is not checked. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.9 Enable data-at-rest encryption in MariaDB

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE VARIABLE_NAME LIKE '%ENCRYPT%' AND VARIABLE_VALUE = 'OFF') = 0 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.INNODB_TABLESPACES_ENCRYPTION) > 0 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.INNODB_TABLESPACES_ENCRYPTION WHERE ENCRYPTION_SCHEME = 0) = 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Configure a key management plugin (e.g. file_key_management with an encrypted key file under /etc/mysql/encryption, mysql:mysql, mode 640), then under [mariadbd] set innodb_encrypt_tables=ON, innodb_encrypt_log=ON, innodb_encrypt_temporary_tables=ON, encrypt_binlog=ON, encrypt_tmp_files=ON, encrypt_tmp_disk_tables=ON, aria_encrypt_tables=ON, innodb_encryption_threads=4; restart, and encrypt backups (e.g. mariabackup | openssl enc).

title: Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The PROCESS privilege found in the mysql.user table determines whether a given user can see statement execution information for all sessions.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure 'PROCESS' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'PROCESS'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE PROCESS ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'SHUTDOWN' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The SHUTDOWN privilege simply enables use of the shutdown option to the mysqladmin command, which allows a user with the SHUTDOWN privilege the ability to shut down the MariaDB server.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5 Ensure 'SHUTDOWN' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'SHUTDOWN'; Ensure only administrative users are returned in the result set.

remediation.command: REVOKE SHUTDOWN ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure 'REPLICATION SLAVE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users
description: The REPLICATION SLAVE privilege governs whether a given user (in the context of the source server) can request updates that have been made on the source server.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.8 Ensure 'REPLICATION SLAVE' is Not Granted to Non-Administrative Users

audit.command: Run SELECT GRANTEE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'REPLICATION SLAVE'; Ensure only accounts designated for replica users are returned.

remediation.command: REVOKE REPLICATION SLAVE ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each non-administrative grantee.

title: Ensure DML/DDL Grants are Limited to Specific Databases and Users
description: DML/DDL includes the set of privileges used to modify or create data structures. This includes INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, CREATE, and ALTER privileges.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.9 Ensure DML/DDL Grants are Limited to Specific Databases and Users

audit.command: Run SELECT User, Host, Db FROM mysql.db WHERE Select_priv='Y' OR Insert_priv='Y' OR Update_priv='Y' OR Delete_priv='Y' OR Create_priv='Y' OR Drop_priv='Y' OR Alter_priv='Y'; and ensure every returned user is permitted these privileges on the indicated database.

remediation.command: REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, ALTER ON <db>.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; for each unauthorized grant.

title: Securely Define Stored Procedures and Functions DEFINER and INVOKER
description: Stored procedure and stored function declarations include a definition of permissions which can be used to escalate permissions. It's important to inspect these settings to ensure they do not unnecessarily escalate privileges.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.10 Securely Define Stored Procedures and Functions DEFINER and INVOKER

audit.command: Run SHOW PROCEDURE STATUS; and SHOW FUNCTION STATUS; and inspect Definer and Security_type. For SQL SECURITY DEFINER routines owned by powerful users, review the code (SHOW CREATE PROCEDURE/FUNCTION <name>) and information_schema.routines/parameters.

remediation.command: Use SQL SECURITY INVOKER where possible, or set DEFINER to a least-privileged account (ALTER/CREATE ... DEFINER=...), and restrict EXECUTE on sensitive routines.

title: Ensure 'log_error' is configured correctly
description: The error log contains information about events such as mariadbd starting and stopping, when a table needs to be checked or repaired, and, depending on the host operating system, stack traces when mariadbd fails. Fails when log_error is empty, stderr or ./stderr.err. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure 'log_error' is configured correctly

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(IFNULL(@@global.log_error, '') NOT IN ('', 'stderr') AND @@global.log_error NOT LIKE '%stderr.err', 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set log_error=<path to error log file> under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure the Audit Plugin Can't be Unloaded
description: Set server_audit to FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5 Ensure the Audit Plugin Can't be Unloaded

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL((SELECT LOAD_OPTION FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_NAME = 'SERVER_AUDIT'), 'NOT_LOADED')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set server_audit=FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure Binary and Relay Logs are Encrypted
description: The encrypt_binlog system variable may be used to configure encryption of the binary and relay logs. This may be configured to ON even if binary logging is not enabled in order to encrypt relay log files. encrypt_binlog also encrypts relay logs. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.6 Ensure Binary and Relay Logs are Encrypted

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.encrypt_binlog = 1, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set encrypt_binlog=ON under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf) (requires a key management plugin), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames
description: MariaDB can make use of host wildcards when granting permissions to users on specific databases. For example, you may grant a given privilege to '<user>'@'%'. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.5 Ensure No Users Have Wildcard Hostnames

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE host = '%'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: For each SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user WHERE host = '%' result: RENAME USER '<user>'@'%' TO '<user>'@'<specific host>'; or DROP USER.

title: Prevent Password Reuse
description: Users should be prevented from reusing past passwords when performing mandatory password changes.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.7 Prevent Password Reuse

audit.command: Run SELECT plugin_status, load_option FROM information_schema.plugins WHERE PLUGIN_NAME = 'password_reuse_check'; It fails if empty, PLUGIN_STATUS is not ACTIVE or LOAD_OPTION is not FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT. Then SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name = 'strict_password_validation'; must be ON (hash passwords would bypass the check).

remediation.command: Under [mariadbd] add plugin_load_add = password_reuse_check, password_reuse_check = FORCE_PLUS_PERMANENT, password_reuse_check_interval = <days> and strict_password_validation = ON, then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure only approved ciphers are used for Replication
description: MariaDB supports multiple encryption ciphers that can be used for TLS connections during replication. Ciphers can vary in strength, speed and overhead.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.4 Ensure only approved ciphers are used for Replication

audit.command: If replication uses TLS, run SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G on the replica and verify Master_SSL_Cipher lists only approved ciphers/cipher suites. An empty value or unapproved ciphers is a fail.

remediation.command: STOP REPLICA; CHANGE MASTER TO MASTER_SSL_CIPHER = '<approved cipher list>'; START REPLICA;

title: Place Databases on Non-System Partitions
description: It is generally accepted that host operating systems should include different filesystem partitions for different purposes. One set of filesystems is typically called system partitions, and these are generally reserved for host system/application operation.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Place Databases on Non-System Partitions

audit.command: Find the data and log locations: SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE (VARIABLE_NAME LIKE '%dir' OR VARIABLE_NAME LIKE '%file') AND VARIABLE_NAME NOT LIKE '%core%'; then run df -h <directory> for datadir and the others. They must not be on the root (/), /var or /usr partitions.

remediation.command: Create a dedicated partition/volume for the data, stop MariaDB, move datadir there (copy preserving ownership mysql:mysql), update datadir in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf) and any SELinux/AppArmor policy, then start MariaDB.

title: Disable MariaDB Command History
description: On Unix, the mysql client writes a record of executed statements to a history file. By default, this file is named .mysql_history and is created in your home directory. To specify a different file, set the value of the MYSQL_HISTFILE environment variable. Run as root; counts client history files under /home and /root that are not symlinks to /dev/null.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Disable MariaDB Command History

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; l=$(find /home /root -maxdepth 4 \( -name .mysql_history -o -name .mariadb_history \) 2>/dev/null); n=0; for x in $l; do [ "$(readlink "$x")" = /dev/null ] || n=$((n+1)); done; echo "$n"

remediation.guidance: For each user remove the history file and prevent re-creation: rm -f ~<user>/.mysql_history && ln -s /dev/null ~<user>/.mysql_history, or export MYSQL_HISTFILE=/dev/null in the shell startup script.

title: Ensure MariaDB is Run Under a Sandbox Environment
description: Use of the chroot() system call at startup, Systemd with settings to achieve isolation, or docker will put MariaDB in a Sandbox environment.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure MariaDB is Run Under a Sandbox Environment

audit.command: Check whether MariaDB is confined: chroot option (grep -r '^chroot' /etc/mysql /etc/my.cnf*; must differ from datadir), systemd unit runs as a non-root user (systemctl status mariadb: Main PID not owned by root), or it runs in a container (docker ps / podman ps). None of these is a fail.

remediation.command: Run MariaDB under systemd as the mysql user, in a container, or with chroot=<path> under [mariadbd], and keep SELinux/AppArmor confinement enabled.

title: Backup of Configuration and Related Files
description: It is important to include configuration, log, key, certificates, and customized files in backups.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.7 Backup of Configuration and Related Files

audit.command: Check that the backup includes: edited configuration files (mariadb.cnf and included files), key management/keyring files, audit log files, SSL certificates and keys, UDF libraries and custom source code.

remediation.command: Add these configuration and related files to the backup set.

title: Dedicate the Machine Running MariaDB
description: It is recommended that MariaDB Server software be installed on a dedicated server. This architectural consideration affords flexibility in that the database server can be placed on a separate zone allowing access only from particular hosts and over particular protocols.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Dedicate the Machine Running MariaDB

audit.command: Verify the host has no other roles and that no applications or services unrelated to MariaDB are installed or running (systemctl list-units --type=service; package list).

remediation.command: Move unrelated services and applications off the MariaDB host.

title: Do Not Reuse Usernames
description: Database user accounts should not be reused for multiple applications or users.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Do Not Reuse Usernames

audit.command: List accounts: SELECT host, user, plugin FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT IN ('mysql','root','mariadb.sys'); Each account must belong to exactly one system account, person or application; shared or reused usernames are a fail.

remediation.command: Create a separate account per person, application and system account, migrate their grants, and drop the shared accounts.

title: Ensure 'sql_mode' Contains 'STRICT_ALL_TABLES'
description: When data changing statements are made (i.e., INSERT, UPDATE), MariaDB can handle invalid or missing values differently depending on whether strict SQL mode is enabled. When strict SQL mode is enabled, data may not be truncated or otherwise "adjusted" to make the data changing statement work. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.8 Ensure 'sql_mode' Contains 'STRICT_ALL_TABLES'

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(FIND_IN_SET('STRICT_ALL_TABLES', @@global.sql_mode) > 0, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Add STRICT_ALL_TABLES to sql_mode under [mariadbd] (e.g. sql_mode=STRICT_ALL_TABLES,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION) after testing applications, then restart or SET GLOBAL sql_mode.

title: Ensure Log Files are Stored on a Non-System Partition
description: MariaDB log files can be set in the MariaDB configuration to exist anywhere on the filesystem. It is common practice to ensure that the system filesystem is left uncluttered by application logs. System filesystems include the root (/), /var, or /usr. Fails when log_bin_basename is under /var or /usr or on the root filesystem; passes when binary logging is off. Run on the database host. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure Log Files are Stored on a Non-System Partition

audit.command: d=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT @@global.datadir" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IFNULL(@@global.log_bin_basename, '')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$b" ] || { echo compliant; exit 0; }; case "$b" in /*) ;; *) b="$d/${b#./}" ;; esac; case "$b" in /var/*|/usr/*) echo "under /var or /usr: $b"; exit 0 ;; esac; m=$(df -P "$(dirname "$b")" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $6}'); [ -n "$m" ] || exit 1; [ "$m" = / ] && echo "on the root filesystem: $b" || echo compliant

remediation.command: Set log_bin=<path on a dedicated, non-system partition> under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf), then restart MariaDB.

title: Ensure 'log_warnings' is Set to '2'
description: The log_warnings system variable, set to 2 by default, specifies the verbosity of events sent to the MariaDB error log. A value of 2 enables logging of error and warning messages, a value of 3 also includes informational logging, a value of 1 logs only errors. Runs mariadb -NBe with the client defaults: as root on the server the unix_socket plugin usually authenticates; otherwise put an administrative account in ~/.my.cnf (mode 0600), not MYSQL_PWD (see 1.4/1.6).
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure 'log_warnings' is Set to '2'

audit.command: out=$(mariadb -NBe "SELECT IF(@@global.log_warnings = 2, 'compliant', 'noncompliant')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Set log_warnings=2 under [mariadbd] in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf.d/server.cnf) (SET GLOBAL log_warnings = 2 applies it now), then restart MariaDB.

title: Set Maximum Connection Limits for Server and per User
description: Limiting concurrent connections to a MariaDB server can be used to reduce risk of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks performed by exhausting connection resources.
reference: CIS MariaDB 10.11 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.3 Set Maximum Connection Limits for Server and per User

audit.command: Run SELECT VARIABLE_NAME, VARIABLE_VALUE FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES WHERE VARIABLE_NAME LIKE 'max_%connections'; (max_user_connections 0 = no limit) and SELECT user, host, max_user_connections FROM mysql.user WHERE user NOT LIKE 'mysql.%' AND user <> 'root'; (0 = global value applies). No server or per-user limit is a fail.

remediation.command: Set max_connections and max_user_connections under [mariadbd] (SET GLOBAL to apply now) and per account with ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' WITH MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS <n>;
